judgement_checks.param_mismatch: Methods: REML random-effects (metafor rma default method=REML), SMD via escalc/rma measure=SMD, I2 from rma, min 4 comparisons not enforced in code but no outcome has <4 studies; code forest.R uses rma(measure='SMD') and rma(yi,vi,method='REML') for between-group. No parameter in the paper contradicts the code.
judgement_checks.figure_data_mismatch: Figure 2-15 are produced by forest.R from data/Ex.vs.NonEx.csv and data/Pre.Post.csv; the stored PNGs in results/ are the authors' own output of that code; Table 1/2 study counts match the number of rows per Outcome in the csv (checked in stage 3/4 recount).

The body sentence about the same quantity (shared words: citrate, heterogeneity, seconds, synthase) gives 58.05: '...We noted no evidence of heterogeneity with the exception of I ^2 statistically significant heterogeneity for STS (seconds) ( I²=58.05%; p=0.04) and citrate synthase ( I²=70.90%; p=0.002) ( Table 2)....'. Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'An individual-participant-data re-analysis of 312 patients from eight of these trials confirmed the VO _2peak benefit (SMD 0.61 [95% CI 0.33, 0.89]).'. Its head count 312 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 're-analysis' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.
